question: Who was the founder of the Widow Remarriage Association (1861)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahadev Govind Ranade**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atma Ram Pandurang **was a social reformer who worked for the upliftment of women and the eradication of the caste system in India. He founded the Prarthana Samaj in 1867.
 
• **Raja Rammohan Roy** was a prominent social reformer and founder of the Brahmo Samaj. He worked for the abolition of Sati and advocated for women's education.
 
• **R.G. Bhandarkar **was a scholar and social reformer who worked for the promotion of education and the eradication of the caste system in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade was a social reformer, scholar, and jurist who played a crucial role in the Widow Remarriage Movement in India. He founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1861 with the aim of promoting the remarriage of widows, which was a taboo in society at that time.
 
• Ranade believed that the remarriage of widows would not only provide them with a new lease of life but also help in the overall progress of society. He also advocated for the education of women and worked for their empowerment.
 
• Ranade's efforts bore fruit when the Widow Remarriage Act was passed in 1856, which legalized the remarriage of widows in India.
 
• Ranade was also a strong advocate of Indian nationalism and worked towards the upliftment of the oppressed classes in society. He was a member of the Indian National Congress and played a crucial role in shaping its agenda.
